previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease was admitted with chest and bilateral knee pain consistent with a vaso-occlusive crisis, triggered by community-acquired pneumonia. She presented with fever, leukocytosis, and a new left lower lobe infiltrate on chest X-ray. She was treated with a seven-day course of levofloxacin, IV fluids, oxygen supplementation, and IV hydromorphone, transitioning to oral pain control by discharge. Her condition improved with resolution of fever, stable hemoglobin without transfusion, and successful weaning from oxygen. She was discharged home in stable condition on her baseline hydroxyurea and folic acid regimen, with instructions to continue oral and intramuscular hydromorphone as needed for pain.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ yo female with SCD and HCV who presents with 
pain crisis in extremities.  
.  
# Sickle cell pain crisis: Patient had her hematocrit trending 
down, low haptoglobin, suggestive of hemolysis.  She recieved 
symptomatic support with IV fluid, Dilaudid, O2 support.  She 
was placed on hydroxyurea, folic acid and B12 supplements.  She 
did not require additional coverage with antibiotics, nor did 
she have any signs of active infection.  She refused 
transfusions.  At the time of discharge, she remained stable in 
good spirits and was given a rapid dilaudid taper. 
.
# Acute Pulmonary edema on CXR: Pt has been sating well despite 
findings of volume overload.  Given chronic anemia, high-output 
heart failure was a concern which was ruled out with 
echocardiogram.  She continued to recieve IVF hydration and did 
not have any signs of acute chest.
. 
# Anemia: Macrocytosis likely secondary to lysis and chronic 
sickle cell disease with increased reticulocytosis, but given 
borderline B12, may have a megaloblastic component.  She was 
given supplements and was managed as outlined above.
.
# Proteinuria: U/A without protein today.  
.  
# Stress: Pt reports employer is understanding of her medical 
issues. Declines SW consult.
